question: Which organ handles oxygen and waste exchange for the developing fetus?
explanation: The fetus is submerged in fluid and cannot breathe air, so the placenta takes over the work of the lungs and kidneys until birth. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why does very little blood flow through the fetal lungs before birth?

options.A: The placenta pumps blood away from the chest
options.B: The fetal trachea is blocked by amniotic fluid
options.C: The pulmonary blood vessels are tightly constricted
options.D: The right side of the heart is completely closed

explanation: Before birth, fluid-filled lungs and tight blood vessels create high resistance, which naturally pushes blood through the fetal shunts instead. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the name of the vessel that carries oxygen-rich blood away from the placenta?
explanation: Unlike adult systemic veins, the umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta straight to the fetal body. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h2)

question: Where does a large portion of the oxygen-rich blood go immediately after traveling up the umbilical vein?

options.A: It flows backward into the amniotic fluid
options.B: It splits, with some going to the liver and the rest bypassing it
options.C: It goes directly into the left ventricle to feed the lungs
options.D: It mixes completely with waste products inside the gut

explanation: The liver requires some blood supply for its own growth, but a major portion is shunted past it to protect the oxygen quality for the brain. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the ductus venosus in the fetus?

options.A: To bypass the liver and direct blood to the inferior vena cava
options.B: To prevent blood from entering the developing brain tissue
options.C: To send deoxygenated blood straight to the placenta for cleansing
options.D: To pump blood directly from the right atrium to the left atrium

explanation: The ductus venosus acts as a shortcut around the liver so oxygenated blood reaches the heart faster with less oxygen loss. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h3)

question: What happens to the ductus venosus after the newborn is delivered and the cord is tied?

options.A: It widens to accommodate the sudden increase in liver size
options.B: It remains open permanently to help with adult digestion
options.C: It closes up and eventually becomes a fibrous ligament
options.D: It turns into an artery supplying the lower extremities

explanation: With the sudden loss of umbilical blood flow, the functional shunt closes and later transforms into connective tissue. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h3)

question: Where is the foramen ovale located within the fetal heart?

options.A: Between the superior vena cava and the right atrium
options.B: Between the right ventricle and the left ventricle
options.C: Between the aorta and the pulmonary artery
options.D: Between the right atrium and the left atrium

explanation: The foramen ovale is an interatrial opening that allows blood to pass directly from the right side of the heart to the left side. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why is the foramen ovale critical for directing blood flow in the fetus?

options.A: It mixes waste products into the blood heading toward the placenta
options.B: It shunts oxygen-rich blood toward the left atrium and away from the lungs
options.C: It increases pressure inside the pulmonary artery to expand lung tissue
options.D: It stops all blood from entering the heart chambers until after birth

explanation: By moving blood directly to the left atrium, the foramen ovale ensures the brain gets the best possible oxygen supply. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which two major vessels are connected by the ductus arteriosus?

options.A: The superior vena cava and the right ventricle
options.B: The pulmonary artery and the aorta
options.C: The umbilical vein and the inferior vena cava
options.D: The right atrium and the left atrium

explanation: The ductus arteriosus links the pulmonary trunk directly to the descending aorta, successfully bypassing the lungs. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the ductus arteriosus during fetal life?

options.A: To divert blood away from the fluid-filled lungs into the aorta
options.B: To pump deoxygenated blood directly back into the placenta
options.C: To prevent blood from flowing backward into the heart ventricles
options.D: To supply the fetal liver with high-pressure nutrients

explanation: Since the lungs do not oxygenate blood before birth, the ductus arteriosus redirects most right ventricular output away from them. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h5)

question: Which body parts receive the highest concentration of oxygen in the fetal circulation?

options.B: The lower limbs and pelvic organs

explanation: Because of how the foramen ovale and ductus venosus route blood, the head and arms get the freshest oxygen supply. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h6)

question: What vessels carry deoxygenated blood away from the fetus back to the placenta?
explanation: Two umbilical arteries carry metabolic waste and deoxygenated blood from the fetus back to the placental villi. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h6)

question: What physical event triggers the immediate functional closure of the foramen ovale after birth?

options.A: An increase in pressure within the left atrium
options.B: The complete disappearance of placental hormones
options.C: The physical clamping of the umbilical cord
options.D: A sudden drop in the baby's body temperature

explanation: When the lungs open up, blood rushes back into the left side of the heart, pushing the flap of the foramen ovale closed. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which factor plays a major role in causing the ductus arteriosus to constrict after birth?

options.A: A sharp increase in blood oxygen levels
options.B: The complete absence of red blood cells
options.C: An increase in placental blood flow
options.D: A massive drop in systemic blood pressure

explanation: The sudden influx of oxygen when the baby breathes air causes the muscular walls of the ductus arteriosus to clamp down. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h7)
